front: How many days of fieldwork must AQA A-level Geography students undertake during the course?
back: Four days
subdeck_path: AQA A-level Geography 7037 – Key content::Geographical skills and fieldwork::Geography fieldwork::3.3.1 Fieldwork requirements

front: Fieldwork for AQA A-level Geography must relate to processes in which two branches of geography?
back: Physical and human geography
subdeck_path: AQA A-level Geography 7037 – Key content::Geographical skills and fieldwork::Geography fieldwork::3.3.1 Fieldwork requirements

front: Must the four days of A-level fieldwork be full days taken away from the local area?
back: No, they are local or further afield, on full or part days
subdeck_path: AQA A-level Geography 7037 – Key content::Geographical skills and fieldwork::Geography fieldwork::3.3.1 Fieldwork requirements

front: By what date must a school send AQA the fieldwork statement confirming students' four days of fieldwork?
back: 15 May in the year of entry
subdeck_path: AQA A-level Geography 7037 – Key content::Geographical skills and fieldwork::Geography fieldwork::3.3.1 Fieldwork requirements

front: Under AQA rules, how is a late or missing fieldwork statement treated?
back: As malpractice or maladministration
subdeck_path: AQA A-level Geography 7037 – Key content::Geographical skills and fieldwork::Geography fieldwork::3.3.1 Fieldwork requirements

front: What is the advisory word count for the AQA A-level Geography NEA independent investigation?
back: 3,000 to 4,000 words
subdeck_path: AQA A-level Geography 7037 – Key content::Geographical skills and fieldwork::Geography fieldwork::3.3.1 Fieldwork requirements

front: How many marks is the AQA A-level Geography NEA (Component 3) worth?
back: 60 marks
subdeck_path: AQA A-level Geography 7037 – Key content::Geographical skills and fieldwork::Geography fieldwork::3.3.1 Fieldwork requirements

front: What percentage of the AQA A-level Geography qualification is the NEA investigation?
subdeck_path: AQA A-level Geography 7037 – Key content::Geographical skills and fieldwork::Geography fieldwork::3.3.1 Fieldwork requirements

front: Who marks the AQA A-level Geography NEA investigation?
back: Teachers, with moderation by AQA
subdeck_path: AQA A-level Geography 7037 – Key content::Geographical skills and fieldwork::Geography fieldwork::3.3.1 Fieldwork requirements

front: What does AQA call the A-level Geography NEA, which must include data collected in the field?
back: The independent investigation (geography fieldwork investigation)
subdeck_path: AQA A-level Geography 7037 – Key content::Geographical skills and fieldwork::Geography fieldwork::3.3.1 Fieldwork requirements

front: Who must define and develop the question or issue for an A-level Geography NEA investigation?
back: The student, individually
subdeck_path: AQA A-level Geography 7037 – Key content::Geographical skills and fieldwork::Geography fieldwork::3.3.1 Fieldwork requirements

front: Can an NEA investigation focus on human geography only, physical only, or a combination?
back: Any of these: human, physical or a combination of both
subdeck_path: AQA A-level Geography 7037 – Key content::Geographical skills and fieldwork::Geography fieldwork::3.3.1 Fieldwork requirements

front: Which part of the A-level Geography specification can an NEA investigation relate to?
back: Any part of the specification content
subdeck_path: AQA A-level Geography 7037 – Key content::Geographical skills and fieldwork::Geography fieldwork::3.3.1 Fieldwork requirements

front: Does the NEA word count include photographs and data presentation such as graphs?
back: Yes, it includes photographs and data presentation (and all text and text boxes)
subdeck_path: AQA A-level Geography 7037 – Key content::Geographical skills and fieldwork::Geography fieldwork::3.3.1 Fieldwork requirements

front: Do appendices count towards the NEA word count?
back: No
subdeck_path: AQA A-level Geography 7037 – Key content::Geographical skills and fieldwork::Geography fieldwork::3.3.1 Fieldwork requirements

front: What should NEA appendices contain, according to AQA?
back: Examples of raw data only, such as one data sheet or questionnaire
subdeck_path: AQA A-level Geography 7037 – Key content::Geographical skills and fieldwork::Geography fieldwork::3.3.1 Fieldwork requirements

front: According to AQA, what is the risk of writing an NEA report below the advisory word count?
back: Not covering the required assessment objectives fully
subdeck_path: AQA A-level Geography 7037 – Key content::Geographical skills and fieldwork::Geography fieldwork::3.3.1 Fieldwork requirements

front: According to AQA, what is the risk of writing an NEA report above the advisory word count?
back: A lack of precision and focus
subdeck_path: AQA A-level Geography 7037 – Key content::Geographical skills and fieldwork::Geography fieldwork::3.3.1 Fieldwork requirements

front: What is the title of NEA mark scheme Area 1?
back: Introduction and preliminary research
subdeck_path: AQA A-level Geography 7037 – Key content::Geographical skills and fieldwork::Geography fieldwork::3.3.1 Fieldwork requirements

front: How many marks is NEA Area 1 (Introduction and preliminary research) worth?
back: 10 marks
subdeck_path: AQA A-level Geography 7037 – Key content::Geographical skills and fieldwork::Geography fieldwork::3.3.1 Fieldwork requirements

front: What is the title of NEA mark scheme Area 2?
back: Methods of field investigation
subdeck_path: AQA A-level Geography 7037 – Key content::Geographical skills and fieldwork::Geography fieldwork::3.3.1 Fieldwork requirements

front: How many marks is NEA Area 2 (Methods of field investigation) worth?
back: 15 marks
subdeck_path: AQA A-level Geography 7037 – Key content::Geographical skills and fieldwork::Geography fieldwork::3.3.1 Fieldwork requirements

front: What is the title of NEA mark scheme Area 3?
back: Methods of critical analysis
subdeck_path: AQA A-level Geography 7037 – Key content::Geographical skills and fieldwork::Geography fieldwork::3.3.1 Fieldwork requirements

front: How many marks is NEA Area 3 (Methods of critical analysis) worth?
back: 20 marks
subdeck_path: AQA A-level Geography 7037 – Key content::Geographical skills and fieldwork::Geography fieldwork::3.3.1 Fieldwork requirements

front: What is the title of NEA mark scheme Area 4?
back: Conclusions, evaluation and presentation
subdeck_path: AQA A-level Geography 7037 – Key content::Geographical skills and fieldwork::Geography fieldwork::3.3.1 Fieldwork requirements

front: How many marks is NEA Area 4 (Conclusions, evaluation and presentation) worth?
back: 15 marks
subdeck_path: AQA A-level Geography 7037 – Key content::Geographical skills and fieldwork::Geography fieldwork::3.3.1 Fieldwork requirements

front: Which assessment objective carries all 10 marks of NEA Area 1?
back: AO3
subdeck_path: AQA A-level Geography 7037 – Key content::Geographical skills and fieldwork::Geography fieldwork::3.3.1 Fieldwork requirements

front: How many of the 20 marks in NEA Area 3 (critical analysis) are AO2?
back: 6 marks (the other 14 are AO3)
subdeck_path: AQA A-level Geography 7037 – Key content::Geographical skills and fieldwork::Geography fieldwork::3.3.1 Fieldwork requirements

front: How many levels does the NEA mark scheme use for each area?
back: Four levels (plus no marks)
subdeck_path: AQA A-level Geography 7037 – Key content::Geographical skills and fieldwork::Geography fieldwork::3.3.1 Fieldwork requirements

front: In NEA Area 1, what must the research question be linked to?
back: The specification
subdeck_path: AQA A-level Geography 7037 – Key content::Geographical skills and fieldwork::Geography fieldwork::3.3.1 Fieldwork requirements

front: In NEA Area 1, what must literature sources be used to set out for the research question?
back: The theoretical or comparative context
subdeck_path: AQA A-level Geography 7037 – Key content::Geographical skills and fieldwork::Geography fieldwork::3.3.1 Fieldwork requirements

front: Which form must accompany each student's NEA, signed by student and teacher to confirm authenticity?
back: The Candidate record form (CRF)
subdeck_path: AQA A-level Geography 7037 – Key content::Geographical skills and fieldwork::Geography fieldwork::3.3.1 Fieldwork requirements

front: Which section of the Candidate record form must the student complete at the planning stage of the NEA?
back: The independent investigation proposal
subdeck_path: AQA A-level Geography 7037 – Key content::Geographical skills and fieldwork::Geography fieldwork::3.3.1 Fieldwork requirements

front: In the NEA, at which stage is collaboration in a group allowed besides exploring possible topics?
back: Collecting field data
subdeck_path: AQA A-level Geography 7037 – Key content::Geographical skills and fieldwork::Geography fieldwork::3.3.1 Fieldwork requirements

front: Must NEA students analyse, present and draw conclusions from their data independently?
back: Yes, these stages must be done independently
subdeck_path: AQA A-level Geography 7037 – Key content::Geographical skills and fieldwork::Geography fieldwork::3.3.1 Fieldwork requirements

front: Can secondary data used in an NEA be supplied by the teacher rather than sourced by the student?
back: No, secondary data must be sourced by the student
subdeck_path: AQA A-level Geography 7037 – Key content::Geographical skills and fieldwork::Geography fieldwork::3.3.1 Fieldwork requirements

front: What must a teacher do if a student gets help beyond general advice on their NEA?
back: Record it on the CRF and take it into account when marking
subdeck_path: AQA A-level Geography 7037 – Key content::Geographical skills and fieldwork::Geography fieldwork::3.3.1 Fieldwork requirements

front: Are teachers allowed to give NEA students a list of titles to choose from?
back: No
subdeck_path: AQA A-level Geography 7037 – Key content::Geographical skills and fieldwork::Geography fieldwork::3.3.1 Fieldwork requirements

front: Are teachers allowed to mark an NEA draft and share the mark so the student can improve it?
back: No
subdeck_path: AQA A-level Geography 7037 – Key content::Geographical skills and fieldwork::Geography fieldwork::3.3.1 Fieldwork requirements

front: According to AQA, which dimension of field research must the NEA evaluation show an understanding of?
back: The ethical dimensions of field research
subdeck_path: AQA A-level Geography 7037 – Key content::Geographical skills and fieldwork::Geography fieldwork::3.3.1 Fieldwork requirements

front: According to AQA, besides a summary of results, what must the NEA conclusion include?
back: The relevance of results to the title and an evaluation of the investigation
subdeck_path: AQA A-level Geography 7037 – Key content::Geographical skills and fieldwork::Geography fieldwork::3.3.1 Fieldwork requirements

front: What is a hypothesis in a geographical investigation?
back: A testable statement predicting a relationship or difference
subdeck_path: AQA A-level Geography 7037 – Key content::Geographical skills and fieldwork::Geography fieldwork::3.3.1 Fieldwork requirements

front: In the fieldwork enquiry process, which stage comes after choosing a question or hypothesis?
back: Planning and collecting data
subdeck_path: AQA A-level Geography 7037 – Key content::Geographical skills and fieldwork::Geography fieldwork::3.3.1 Fieldwork requirements

front: In the fieldwork enquiry process, which stage follows data presentation?
back: Analysis and interpretation of the data
subdeck_path: AQA A-level Geography 7037 – Key content::Geographical skills and fieldwork::Geography fieldwork::3.3.1 Fieldwork requirements

front: What is the final stage of the fieldwork enquiry process?
back: Evaluation of the investigation
subdeck_path: AQA A-level Geography 7037 – Key content::Geographical skills and fieldwork::Geography fieldwork::3.3.1 Fieldwork requirements

front: What is the purpose of a literature review at the start of an investigation?
back: To set the question in its theoretical and comparative context
subdeck_path: AQA A-level Geography 7037 – Key content::Geographical skills and fieldwork::Geography fieldwork::3.3.1 Fieldwork requirements

front: What is a pilot study in fieldwork?
back: A small trial run to test methods before the main data collection
subdeck_path: AQA A-level Geography 7037 – Key content::Geographical skills and fieldwork::Geography fieldwork::3.3.1 Fieldwork requirements

front: What is primary data?
back: Data collected first-hand by the investigator
subdeck_path: AQA A-level Geography 7037 – Key content::Geographical skills and fieldwork::Geography fieldwork::3.3.1 Fieldwork requirements

front: What is secondary data?
back: Data collected by someone else, such as census data or published reports
subdeck_path: AQA A-level Geography 7037 – Key content::Geographical skills and fieldwork::Geography fieldwork::3.3.1 Fieldwork requirements

front: Give one strength of primary data for an investigation.
back: The investigator controls how, where and when it is collected
subdeck_path: AQA A-level Geography 7037 – Key content::Geographical skills and fieldwork::Geography fieldwork::3.3.1 Fieldwork requirements

front: Give one strength of secondary data for an investigation.
back: It covers larger areas or longer time periods than a student could collect
subdeck_path: AQA A-level Geography 7037 – Key content::Geographical skills and fieldwork::Geography fieldwork::3.3.1 Fieldwork requirements

front: What is quantitative data?
back: Numerical data that can be measured or counted
subdeck_path: AQA A-level Geography 7037 – Key content::Geographical skills and fieldwork::Geography fieldwork::3.3.1 Fieldwork requirements

front: What is qualitative data?
back: Non-numerical data such as opinions, descriptions, photos or interview text
subdeck_path: AQA A-level Geography 7037 – Key content::Geographical skills and fieldwork::Geography fieldwork::3.3.1 Fieldwork requirements

front: Give one strength of quantitative data.
back: It can be tested statistically
subdeck_path: AQA A-level Geography 7037 – Key content::Geographical skills and fieldwork::Geography fieldwork::3.3.1 Fieldwork requirements

front: Give one strength of qualitative data.
back: It gives depth, such as people's feelings and meanings
subdeck_path: AQA A-level Geography 7037 – Key content::Geographical skills and fieldwork::Geography fieldwork::3.3.1 Fieldwork requirements

front: What is a population in sampling terms?
back: The whole group or area that the investigation is about
subdeck_path: AQA A-level Geography 7037 – Key content::Geographical skills and fieldwork::Geography fieldwork::3.3.1 Fieldwork requirements

front: Why do geographers sample rather than measure everything?
back: It saves time and money when measuring everything is impossible
subdeck_path: AQA A-level Geography 7037 – Key content::Geographical skills and fieldwork::Geography fieldwork::3.3.1 Fieldwork requirements

front: What is random sampling?
back: Every member or point has an equal chance of being chosen
subdeck_path: AQA A-level Geography 7037 – Key content::Geographical skills and fieldwork::Geography fieldwork::3.3.1 Fieldwork requirements

front: How are sample points chosen in random sampling?
back: Using random number tables or a random number generator
subdeck_path: AQA A-level Geography 7037 – Key content::Geographical skills and fieldwork::Geography fieldwork::3.3.1 Fieldwork requirements

front: Give one strength of random sampling.
back: It avoids investigator bias
subdeck_path: AQA A-level Geography 7037 – Key content::Geographical skills and fieldwork::Geography fieldwork::3.3.1 Fieldwork requirements

front: Give one limitation of random sampling.
back: Parts of the area are often missed or under-represented by chance
subdeck_path: AQA A-level Geography 7037 – Key content::Geographical skills and fieldwork::Geography fieldwork::3.3.1 Fieldwork requirements

front: What is systematic sampling?
back: Choosing samples at regular intervals, such as every 10 m or every 5th person
subdeck_path: AQA A-level Geography 7037 – Key content::Geographical skills and fieldwork::Geography fieldwork::3.3.1 Fieldwork requirements

front: Give one strength of systematic sampling.
back: It is quick and gives even coverage of the area
subdeck_path: AQA A-level Geography 7037 – Key content::Geographical skills and fieldwork::Geography fieldwork::3.3.1 Fieldwork requirements

front: Give one limitation of systematic sampling.
back: It is biased if a pattern in the area matches the sampling interval
subdeck_path: AQA A-level Geography 7037 – Key content::Geographical skills and fieldwork::Geography fieldwork::3.3.1 Fieldwork requirements

front: What is stratified sampling?
back: Sampling each subgroup in proportion to its share of the population
subdeck_path: AQA A-level Geography 7037 – Key content::Geographical skills and fieldwork::Geography fieldwork::3.3.1 Fieldwork requirements

front: Give one strength of stratified sampling.
back: Every subgroup is represented in its correct proportion
subdeck_path: AQA A-level Geography 7037 – Key content::Geographical skills and fieldwork::Geography fieldwork::3.3.1 Fieldwork requirements

front: Give one limitation of stratified sampling.
back: You must know the size of each subgroup in advance
subdeck_path: AQA A-level Geography 7037 – Key content::Geographical skills and fieldwork::Geography fieldwork::3.3.1 Fieldwork requirements

front: A population is 60% female and 40% male. How many males should a stratified sample of 50 include?
subdeck_path: AQA A-level Geography 7037 – Key content::Geographical skills and fieldwork::Geography fieldwork::3.3.1 Fieldwork requirements

front: What is opportunistic (convenience) sampling?
back: Sampling whoever or whatever is easiest to reach at the time
subdeck_path: AQA A-level Geography 7037 – Key content::Geographical skills and fieldwork::Geography fieldwork::3.3.1 Fieldwork requirements

front: Give one limitation of opportunistic sampling.
back: It is biased and unlikely to be representative
subdeck_path: AQA A-level Geography 7037 – Key content::Geographical skills and fieldwork::Geography fieldwork::3.3.1 Fieldwork requirements

front: What is point sampling?
back: Taking measurements at chosen individual points
subdeck_path: AQA A-level Geography 7037 – Key content::Geographical skills and fieldwork::Geography fieldwork::3.3.1 Fieldwork requirements

front: What is line sampling?
back: Taking measurements along a line, such as a transect
subdeck_path: AQA A-level Geography 7037 – Key content::Geographical skills and fieldwork::Geography fieldwork::3.3.1 Fieldwork requirements

front: What is area sampling?
back: Taking measurements within a defined area, such as a quadrat
subdeck_path: AQA A-level Geography 7037 – Key content::Geographical skills and fieldwork::Geography fieldwork::3.3.1 Fieldwork requirements

front: What is a transect in fieldwork?
back: A line across an area along which measurements are taken
subdeck_path: AQA A-level Geography 7037 – Key content::Geographical skills and fieldwork::Geography fieldwork::3.3.1 Fieldwork requirements

front: What is a quadrat?
back: A square frame used to sample an area, such as for vegetation cover
subdeck_path: AQA A-level Geography 7037 – Key content::Geographical skills and fieldwork::Geography fieldwork::3.3.1 Fieldwork requirements

front: What is a risk assessment in fieldwork?
back: Identifying hazards, how likely they are and how to reduce them
subdeck_path: AQA A-level Geography 7037 – Key content::Geographical skills and fieldwork::Geography fieldwork::3.3.1 Fieldwork requirements

front: In a risk assessment, what is a hazard?
back: Something that could cause harm, such as tides or traffic
subdeck_path: AQA A-level Geography 7037 – Key content::Geographical skills and fieldwork::Geography fieldwork::3.3.1 Fieldwork requirements

front: What is informed consent in fieldwork with people?
back: Participants agree after being told the purpose and use of the research
subdeck_path: AQA A-level Geography 7037 – Key content::Geographical skills and fieldwork::Geography fieldwork::3.3.1 Fieldwork requirements

front: What is anonymity in fieldwork with people?
back: Participants' names and identities are not recorded or revealed
subdeck_path: AQA A-level Geography 7037 – Key content::Geographical skills and fieldwork::Geography fieldwork::3.3.1 Fieldwork requirements

front: What is confidentiality in fieldwork with people?
back: Information given is kept private and only used as agreed
subdeck_path: AQA A-level Geography 7037 – Key content::Geographical skills and fieldwork::Geography fieldwork::3.3.1 Fieldwork requirements

front: What is the right to withdraw in fieldwork with people?
back: Participants can stop taking part and have their data removed
subdeck_path: AQA A-level Geography 7037 – Key content::Geographical skills and fieldwork::Geography fieldwork::3.3.1 Fieldwork requirements

front: What makes data geographical?
back: It is linked to a location (spatially referenced)
subdeck_path: AQA A-level Geography 7037 – Key content::Geographical skills and fieldwork::Geographical skills checklist::3.4.1 Qualitative skills and quantitative skills

front: What is coding when analysing qualitative data?
back: Sorting text or images into categories or themes so they can be analysed
subdeck_path: AQA A-level Geography 7037 – Key content::Geographical skills and fieldwork::Geographical skills checklist::3.4.1 Qualitative skills and quantitative skills

front: Why does coding qualitative data actively shape a geographical representation?
back: The researcher chooses the categories, so their choices shape the result
subdeck_path: AQA A-level Geography 7037 – Key content::Geographical skills and fieldwork::Geographical skills checklist::3.4.1 Qualitative skills and quantitative skills

front: Give one limitation of coding qualitative data.
back: It is subjective, so different researchers code the same text differently
subdeck_path: AQA A-level Geography 7037 – Key content::Geographical skills and fieldwork::Geographical skills checklist::3.4.1 Qualitative skills and quantitative skills

front: What is a structured interview?
back: An interview with fixed questions asked in the same order to everyone
subdeck_path: AQA A-level Geography 7037 – Key content::Geographical skills and fieldwork::Geographical skills checklist::3.4.1 Qualitative skills and quantitative skills

front: What is a semi-structured interview?
back: An interview with set questions plus freedom to follow up answers
subdeck_path: AQA A-level Geography 7037 – Key content::Geographical skills and fieldwork::Geographical skills checklist::3.4.1 Qualitative skills and quantitative skills

front: Give one strength of a semi-structured interview over a questionnaire.
back: It allows follow-up questions that give more depth
subdeck_path: AQA A-level Geography 7037 – Key content::Geographical skills and fieldwork::Geographical skills checklist::3.4.1 Qualitative skills and quantitative skills

front: What is an open question?
back: A question that lets the respondent answer in their own words
subdeck_path: AQA A-level Geography 7037 – Key content::Geographical skills and fieldwork::Geographical skills checklist::3.4.1 Qualitative skills and quantitative skills

front: What is a closed question?
back: A question with fixed answer options, such as yes/no or tick boxes
subdeck_path: AQA A-level Geography 7037 – Key content::Geographical skills and fieldwork::Geographical skills checklist::3.4.1 Qualitative skills and quantitative skills

front: Give one strength of closed questions.
back: Answers are easy to count and compare
subdeck_path: AQA A-level Geography 7037 – Key content::Geographical skills and fieldwork::Geographical skills checklist::3.4.1 Qualitative skills and quantitative skills

front: Give one limitation of closed questions.
back: They limit answers to the options given, so detail is lost
subdeck_path: AQA A-level Geography 7037 – Key content::Geographical skills and fieldwork::Geographical skills checklist::3.4.1 Qualitative skills and quantitative skills

front: What is a Likert scale?
back: A scale where respondents rate agreement, such as from 1 to 5
subdeck_path: AQA A-level Geography 7037 – Key content::Geographical skills and fieldwork::Geographical skills checklist::3.4.1 Qualitative skills and quantitative skills

front: What is a bipolar survey, such as an environmental quality survey?
back: Scoring a site between two opposite words, such as -3 (ugly) to +3 (attractive)
subdeck_path: AQA A-level Geography 7037 – Key content::Geographical skills and fieldwork::Geographical skills checklist::3.4.1 Qualitative skills and quantitative skills

front: Give one limitation of a bipolar environmental quality survey.
back: Scores are subjective and differ between observers
subdeck_path: AQA A-level Geography 7037 – Key content::Geographical skills and fieldwork::Geographical skills checklist::3.4.1 Qualitative skills and quantitative skills

front: What is a socio-political implication of representing data about a community?
back: Negative representations can stigmatise the community
subdeck_path: AQA A-level Geography 7037 – Key content::Geographical skills and fieldwork::Geographical skills checklist::3.4.1 Qualitative skills and quantitative skills

front: What is the difference between accuracy and precision in measurement?
back: Accuracy is closeness to the true value, precision is how close repeat readings are
subdeck_path: AQA A-level Geography 7037 – Key content::Geographical skills and fieldwork::Geographical skills checklist::3.4.1 Qualitative skills and quantitative skills

front: What is reliability in fieldwork data?
back: Getting the same results if the method is repeated
subdeck_path: AQA A-level Geography 7037 – Key content::Geographical skills and fieldwork::Geographical skills checklist::3.4.1 Qualitative skills and quantitative skills

front: What is a systematic error?
back: An error that shifts every reading the same way, such as a badly zeroed scale
subdeck_path: AQA A-level Geography 7037 – Key content::Geographical skills and fieldwork::Geographical skills checklist::3.4.1 Qualitative skills and quantitative skills

front: What is a random error?
back: An unpredictable error that varies from reading to reading
subdeck_path: AQA A-level Geography 7037 – Key content::Geographical skills and fieldwork::Geographical skills checklist::3.4.1 Qualitative skills and quantitative skills

front: What is an anomaly (outlier) in a data set?
back: A value that does not fit the overall pattern
subdeck_path: AQA A-level Geography 7037 – Key content::Geographical skills and fieldwork::Geographical skills checklist::3.4.1 Qualitative skills and quantitative skills

front: What do descriptive statistics do?
back: Summarise a data set, such as its average and spread
subdeck_path: AQA A-level Geography 7037 – Key content::Geographical skills and fieldwork::Geographical skills checklist::3.4.1 Qualitative skills and quantitative skills

front: What do inferential statistics do?
back: Test whether a result is significant or likely due to chance
subdeck_path: AQA A-level Geography 7037 – Key content::Geographical skills and fieldwork::Geographical skills checklist::3.4.1 Qualitative skills and quantitative skills

front: What is a measure of central tendency?
back: A single value representing the middle or typical value, such as the mean
subdeck_path: AQA A-level Geography 7037 – Key content::Geographical skills and fieldwork::Geographical skills checklist::3.4.1 Qualitative skills and quantitative skills

front: What is a measure of dispersion?
back: A measure of how spread out the data are, such as the range
subdeck_path: AQA A-level Geography 7037 – Key content::Geographical skills and fieldwork::Geographical skills checklist::3.4.1 Qualitative skills and quantitative skills

front: What is a relational statistic?
back: A test of the relationship between two variables, such as Spearman's rank
subdeck_path: AQA A-level Geography 7037 – Key content::Geographical skills and fieldwork::Geographical skills checklist::3.4.1 Qualitative skills and quantitative skills

front: What is nominal data?
back: Data in named categories with no order, such as land use type
subdeck_path: AQA A-level Geography 7037 – Key content::Geographical skills and fieldwork::Geographical skills checklist::3.4.1 Qualitative skills and quantitative skills

front: What is ordinal data?
back: Data that can be put in rank order
subdeck_path: AQA A-level Geography 7037 – Key content::Geographical skills and fieldwork::Geographical skills checklist::3.4.1 Qualitative skills and quantitative skills

front: What is interval or ratio data?
back: Measured numerical data on a scale with equal intervals
subdeck_path: AQA A-level Geography 7037 – Key content::Geographical skills and fieldwork::Geographical skills checklist::3.4.1 Qualitative skills and quantitative skills

front: What is a base map?
back: A simple outline map onto which data are added
subdeck_path: AQA A-level Geography 7037 – Key content::Geographical skills and fieldwork::Geographical skills checklist::3.4.2.1 Core skills

front: What is a sketch map?
back: A simple hand-drawn map showing the main features of an area
subdeck_path: AQA A-level Geography 7037 – Key content::Geographical skills and fieldwork::Geographical skills checklist::3.4.2.1 Core skills

front: What is a field sketch?
back: A labelled drawing of a view made in the field
subdeck_path: AQA A-level Geography 7037 – Key content::Geographical skills and fieldwork::Geographical skills checklist::3.4.2.1 Core skills

front: Why is annotation better than labelling on a field sketch or photo?
back: Annotations explain features, labels only name them
subdeck_path: AQA A-level Geography 7037 – Key content::Geographical skills and fieldwork::Geographical skills checklist::3.4.2.1 Core skills

front: What is an overlay in mapping?
back: A transparent layer placed over a map to compare data
subdeck_path: AQA A-level Geography 7037 – Key content::Geographical skills and fieldwork::Geographical skills checklist::3.4.2.1 Core skills

front: What is an electronic overlay?
back: A data layer laid over another in GIS software
subdeck_path: AQA A-level Geography 7037 – Key content::Geographical skills and fieldwork::Geographical skills checklist::3.4.2.1 Core skills

front: On an Ordnance Survey map, which is read first in a grid reference: eastings or northings?
back: Eastings
subdeck_path: AQA A-level Geography 7037 – Key content::Geographical skills and fieldwork::Geographical skills checklist::3.4.2.1 Core skills

front: What area does a 4-figure grid reference identify?
back: One 1 km grid square
subdeck_path: AQA A-level Geography 7037 – Key content::Geographical skills and fieldwork::Geographical skills checklist::3.4.2.1 Core skills

front: To what precision does a 6-figure grid reference locate a point?
back: To the nearest 100 m
subdeck_path: AQA A-level Geography 7037 – Key content::Geographical skills and fieldwork::Geographical skills checklist::3.4.2.1 Core skills

front: On a 1:25,000 map, how many centimetres represent 1 km?
back: 4 cm
subdeck_path: AQA A-level Geography 7037 – Key content::Geographical skills and fieldwork::Geographical skills checklist::3.4.2.1 Core skills

front: On a 1:50,000 map, how many centimetres represent 1 km?
back: 2 cm
subdeck_path: AQA A-level Geography 7037 – Key content::Geographical skills and fieldwork::Geographical skills checklist::3.4.2.1 Core skills

front: On an OS map, what are contour lines?
back: Lines joining points of equal height above sea level
subdeck_path: AQA A-level Geography 7037 – Key content::Geographical skills and fieldwork::Geographical skills checklist::3.4.2.1 Core skills

front: On an OS map, what do contour lines close together show?
back: Steep ground
subdeck_path: AQA A-level Geography 7037 – Key content::Geographical skills and fieldwork::Geographical skills checklist::3.4.2.1 Core skills

front: What is a spot height on an OS map?
back: A dot with a number giving the exact height at that point
subdeck_path: AQA A-level Geography 7037 – Key content::Geographical skills and fieldwork::Geographical skills checklist::3.4.2.1 Core skills

front: What is the benefit of using OS maps at a larger scale such as 1:25,000?
back: More detail is shown
subdeck_path: AQA A-level Geography 7037 – Key content::Geographical skills and fieldwork::Geographical skills checklist::3.4.2.1 Core skills

front: What is geo-located (geotagged) data?
back: Data with location coordinates attached, such as a geotagged photo
subdeck_path: AQA A-level Geography 7037 – Key content::Geographical skills and fieldwork::Geographical skills checklist::3.4.2.1 Core skills

front: What is a questionnaire?
back: A set of written questions given to many people to collect comparable data
subdeck_path: AQA A-level Geography 7037 – Key content::Geographical skills and fieldwork::Geographical skills checklist::3.4.2.1 Core skills

front: Why should a questionnaire be piloted before use?
back: To find unclear or biased questions
subdeck_path: AQA A-level Geography 7037 – Key content::Geographical skills and fieldwork::Geographical skills checklist::3.4.2.1 Core skills

front: What is a leading question?
back: A question worded to push the respondent towards an answer
subdeck_path: AQA A-level Geography 7037 – Key content::Geographical skills and fieldwork::Geographical skills checklist::3.4.2.1 Core skills

front: What is a choropleth map?
back: A map with areas shaded by value, darker shades for higher values
subdeck_path: AQA A-level Geography 7037 – Key content::Geographical skills and fieldwork::Geographical skills checklist::3.4.2.2 Cartographic skills

front: What kind of data should be used for a choropleth map: raw totals or values per area?
back: Values per area, such as densities or percentages
subdeck_path: AQA A-level Geography 7037 – Key content::Geographical skills and fieldwork::Geographical skills checklist::3.4.2.2 Cartographic skills

front: Give one limitation of a choropleth map.
back: It suggests a uniform value across each area and sudden changes at boundaries
subdeck_path: AQA A-level Geography 7037 – Key content::Geographical skills and fieldwork::Geographical skills checklist::3.4.2.2 Cartographic skills

front: What is an isoline map?
back: A map with lines joining places of equal value
subdeck_path: AQA A-level Geography 7037 – Key content::Geographical skills and fieldwork::Geographical skills checklist::3.4.2.2 Cartographic skills

front: What are isolines of equal pressure called?
back: Isobars
subdeck_path: AQA A-level Geography 7037 – Key content::Geographical skills and fieldwork::Geographical skills checklist::3.4.2.2 Cartographic skills

front: What are isolines of equal temperature called?
back: Isotherms
subdeck_path: AQA A-level Geography 7037 – Key content::Geographical skills and fieldwork::Geographical skills checklist::3.4.2.2 Cartographic skills

front: What kind of data does an isoline map need?
back: Continuous data that changes gradually across space
subdeck_path: AQA A-level Geography 7037 – Key content::Geographical skills and fieldwork::Geographical skills checklist::3.4.2.2 Cartographic skills

front: Give one limitation of an isoline map.
back: Lines are estimated between data points, so they are inaccurate where points are few
subdeck_path: AQA A-level Geography 7037 – Key content::Geographical skills and fieldwork::Geographical skills checklist::3.4.2.2 Cartographic skills

front: What is a dot map?
back: A map where each dot represents a fixed quantity
subdeck_path: AQA A-level Geography 7037 – Key content::Geographical skills and fieldwork::Geographical skills checklist::3.4.2.2 Cartographic skills

front: Give one strength of a dot map.
back: It shows distribution and density clearly
subdeck_path: AQA A-level Geography 7037 – Key content::Geographical skills and fieldwork::Geographical skills checklist::3.4.2.2 Cartographic skills

front: Give one limitation of a dot map.
back: Dots merge in dense areas so they are hard to count
subdeck_path: AQA A-level Geography 7037 – Key content::Geographical skills and fieldwork::Geographical skills checklist::3.4.2.2 Cartographic skills

front: What is a flow-line map?
back: A map with lines along routes, their width proportional to the amount of movement
subdeck_path: AQA A-level Geography 7037 – Key content::Geographical skills and fieldwork::Geographical skills checklist::3.4.2.2 Cartographic skills

front: What is a desire-line map?
back: Straight lines from origin to destination showing movement, not the actual route
subdeck_path: AQA A-level Geography 7037 – Key content::Geographical skills and fieldwork::Geographical skills checklist::3.4.2.2 Cartographic skills

front: What does each line show on a trip-line map?
back: One individual journey from origin to destination
subdeck_path: AQA A-level Geography 7037 – Key content::Geographical skills and fieldwork::Geographical skills checklist::3.4.2.2 Cartographic skills

front: What is a proportional symbol map?
back: A map with symbols whose size is proportional to the value at each place
subdeck_path: AQA A-level Geography 7037 – Key content::Geographical skills and fieldwork::Geographical skills checklist::3.4.2.2 Cartographic skills

front: For proportional circles, what is made proportional to the value?
back: The area of the circle
subdeck_path: AQA A-level Geography 7037 – Key content::Geographical skills and fieldwork::Geographical skills checklist::3.4.2.2 Cartographic skills

front: Give one limitation of proportional symbols.
back: Large symbols overlap and hide each other or the map
subdeck_path: AQA A-level Geography 7037 – Key content::Geographical skills and fieldwork::Geographical skills checklist::3.4.2.2 Cartographic skills

front: What is a located graph?
back: A graph placed on a map at the location its data refer to
subdeck_path: AQA A-level Geography 7037 – Key content::Geographical skills and fieldwork::Geographical skills checklist::3.4.2.2 Cartographic skills

front: What is a synoptic chart?
back: A weather map showing pressure, fronts and weather at one time
subdeck_path: AQA A-level Geography 7037 – Key content::Geographical skills and fieldwork::Geographical skills checklist::3.4.2.2 Cartographic skills

front: On a synoptic chart, what do closely spaced isobars show?
back: Strong winds
subdeck_path: AQA A-level Geography 7037 – Key content::Geographical skills and fieldwork::Geographical skills checklist::3.4.2.2 Cartographic skills

front: On a synoptic chart, what is shown by isobars around low pressure?
back: A depression
subdeck_path: AQA A-level Geography 7037 – Key content::Geographical skills and fieldwork::Geographical skills checklist::3.4.2.2 Cartographic skills

front: On a synoptic chart, what is shown by isobars around high pressure?
back: An anticyclone
subdeck_path: AQA A-level Geography 7037 – Key content::Geographical skills and fieldwork::Geographical skills checklist::3.4.2.2 Cartographic skills

front: What is an atlas map?
back: A small-scale map showing patterns over large areas, such as countries
subdeck_path: AQA A-level Geography 7037 – Key content::Geographical skills and fieldwork::Geographical skills checklist::3.4.2.2 Cartographic skills

front: Which graph type shows continuous change over time?
back: A line graph
subdeck_path: AQA A-level Geography 7037 – Key content::Geographical skills and fieldwork::Geographical skills checklist::3.4.2.3 Graphical skills

front: What is a compound line graph?
back: Lines stacked so each band shows one part and the top line shows the total
subdeck_path: AQA A-level Geography 7037 – Key content::Geographical skills and fieldwork::Geographical skills checklist::3.4.2.3 Graphical skills

front: What is a comparative bar graph?
back: Bars for two or more data sets drawn side by side to compare
subdeck_path: AQA A-level Geography 7037 – Key content::Geographical skills and fieldwork::Geographical skills checklist::3.4.2.3 Graphical skills

front: What is a compound (divided) bar graph?
back: A bar split into parts that make up the total
subdeck_path: AQA A-level Geography 7037 – Key content::Geographical skills and fieldwork::Geographical skills checklist::3.4.2.3 Graphical skills

front: What is a divergent bar graph?
back: Bars drawn above and below (or either side of) a central zero line
subdeck_path: AQA A-level Geography 7037 – Key content::Geographical skills and fieldwork::Geographical skills checklist::3.4.2.3 Graphical skills

front: When is a divergent graph used?
back: For data with positive and negative values, such as bipolar scores
subdeck_path: AQA A-level Geography 7037 – Key content::Geographical skills and fieldwork::Geographical skills checklist::3.4.2.3 Graphical skills

front: What does a scatter graph show?
back: The relationship between two variables
subdeck_path: AQA A-level Geography 7037 – Key content::Geographical skills and fieldwork::Geographical skills checklist::3.4.2.3 Graphical skills

front: On a scatter graph, which axis is the independent variable plotted on?
back: The x (horizontal) axis
subdeck_path: AQA A-level Geography 7037 – Key content::Geographical skills and fieldwork::Geographical skills checklist::3.4.2.3 Graphical skills

front: What does a best fit line on a scatter graph show?
back: The trend of the relationship
subdeck_path: AQA A-level Geography 7037 – Key content::Geographical skills and fieldwork::Geographical skills checklist::3.4.2.3 Graphical skills

front: Through which point should a best fit line pass?
back: The mean point (mean of x, mean of y)
subdeck_path: AQA A-level Geography 7037 – Key content::Geographical skills and fieldwork::Geographical skills checklist::3.4.2.3 Graphical skills

front: What does a best fit line rising from left to right show?
back: A positive correlation
subdeck_path: AQA A-level Geography 7037 – Key content::Geographical skills and fieldwork::Geographical skills checklist::3.4.2.3 Graphical skills

front: What does a best fit line falling from left to right show?
back: A negative correlation
subdeck_path: AQA A-level Geography 7037 – Key content::Geographical skills and fieldwork::Geographical skills checklist::3.4.2.3 Graphical skills

front: Does a strong correlation on a scatter graph prove that one variable causes the other?
back: No, correlation does not prove causation
subdeck_path: AQA A-level Geography 7037 – Key content::Geographical skills and fieldwork::Geographical skills checklist::3.4.2.3 Graphical skills

front: When is a logarithmic scale used on a graph?
back: When data cover a very large range of values
subdeck_path: AQA A-level Geography 7037 – Key content::Geographical skills and fieldwork::Geographical skills checklist::3.4.2.3 Graphical skills

front: On a logarithmic scale, what happens to values with each cycle?
back: They increase tenfold (x10)
subdeck_path: AQA A-level Geography 7037 – Key content::Geographical skills and fieldwork::Geographical skills checklist::3.4.2.3 Graphical skills

front: What is a semi-logarithmic graph?
back: A graph with one log axis and one normal (arithmetic) axis
subdeck_path: AQA A-level Geography 7037 – Key content::Geographical skills and fieldwork::Geographical skills checklist::3.4.2.3 Graphical skills

front: Which value is impossible to plot on a logarithmic scale?
back: Zero
subdeck_path: AQA A-level Geography 7037 – Key content::Geographical skills and fieldwork::Geographical skills checklist::3.4.2.3 Graphical skills

front: What is a triangular graph used for?
back: Three variables that add up to 100%
subdeck_path: AQA A-level Geography 7037 – Key content::Geographical skills and fieldwork::Geographical skills checklist::3.4.2.3 Graphical skills

front: Which classic data set is plotted on a triangular graph in physical geography?
back: Soil or sediment texture (sand, silt and clay)
subdeck_path: AQA A-level Geography 7037 – Key content::Geographical skills and fieldwork::Geographical skills checklist::3.4.2.3 Graphical skills

front: How many degrees of a pie chart represent 25% of the total?
back: 90 degrees
subdeck_path: AQA A-level Geography 7037 – Key content::Geographical skills and fieldwork::Geographical skills checklist::3.4.2.3 Graphical skills

front: How do you convert a percentage to degrees for a pie chart?
back: Multiply by 3.6
subdeck_path: AQA A-level Geography 7037 – Key content::Geographical skills and fieldwork::Geographical skills checklist::3.4.2.3 Graphical skills

front: What is a proportional divided circle?
back: A pie chart whose circle area is proportional to the total
subdeck_path: AQA A-level Geography 7037 – Key content::Geographical skills and fieldwork::Geographical skills checklist::3.4.2.3 Graphical skills

front: For proportional circles, the circle radius is proportional to what?
back: The square root of the value
subdeck_path: AQA A-level Geography 7037 – Key content::Geographical skills and fieldwork::Geographical skills checklist::3.4.2.3 Graphical skills

front: One proportional circle shows 400, another 100. How many times larger is the first circle's radius?
back: 2 times (square root of 4)
subdeck_path: AQA A-level Geography 7037 – Key content::Geographical skills and fieldwork::Geographical skills checklist::3.4.2.3 Graphical skills

front: What is a dispersion diagram?
back: Individual values plotted as dots along a vertical scale to show spread
subdeck_path: AQA A-level Geography 7037 – Key content::Geographical skills and fieldwork::Geographical skills checklist::3.4.2.3 Graphical skills

front: Which statistics are read easily from a dispersion diagram?
back: The median and interquartile range
subdeck_path: AQA A-level Geography 7037 – Key content::Geographical skills and fieldwork::Geographical skills checklist::3.4.2.3 Graphical skills

front: What does a kite diagram show?
back: Abundance or cover of species along a transect
subdeck_path: AQA A-level Geography 7037 – Key content::Geographical skills and fieldwork::Geographical skills checklist::3.4.2.3 Graphical skills

front: Where is a kite diagram commonly used in physical geography fieldwork?
back: Vegetation succession across sand dunes
subdeck_path: AQA A-level Geography 7037 – Key content::Geographical skills and fieldwork::Geographical skills checklist::3.4.2.3 Graphical skills

front: What does a rose diagram show?
back: Direction and frequency, such as wind direction
subdeck_path: AQA A-level Geography 7037 – Key content::Geographical skills and fieldwork::Geographical skills checklist::3.4.2.3 Graphical skills

front: Besides wind direction, name one use of a rose diagram in geography.
back: Pebble (clast) orientation (also: corrie aspect)
subdeck_path: AQA A-level Geography 7037 – Key content::Geographical skills and fieldwork::Geographical skills checklist::3.4.2.3 Graphical skills

front: What does a Lorenz curve plot?
back: Cumulative % of a variable against cumulative % of the population
subdeck_path: AQA A-level Geography 7037 – Key content::Geographical skills and fieldwork::Geographical skills checklist::3.4.2.3 Graphical skills

front: What does the straight diagonal line on a Lorenz curve graph represent?
back: Perfect equality
subdeck_path: AQA A-level Geography 7037 – Key content::Geographical skills and fieldwork::Geographical skills checklist::3.4.2.3 Graphical skills

front: On a Lorenz curve, what does a curve far from the diagonal show?
back: High inequality (uneven distribution)
subdeck_path: AQA A-level Geography 7037 – Key content::Geographical skills and fieldwork::Geographical skills checklist::3.4.2.3 Graphical skills

front: What does a box and whisker plot show?
back: Median, quartiles and range of a data set
subdeck_path: AQA A-level Geography 7037 – Key content::Geographical skills and fieldwork::Geographical skills checklist::3.4.2.3 Graphical skills

front: How is the mean calculated?
back: Add all the values and divide by the number of values
subdeck_path: AQA A-level Geography 7037 – Key content::Geographical skills and fieldwork::Geographical skills checklist::3.4.2.4 Statistical skills

front: What is the median?
back: The middle value when data are in rank order
subdeck_path: AQA A-level Geography 7037 – Key content::Geographical skills and fieldwork::Geographical skills checklist::3.4.2.4 Statistical skills

front: What is the mode?
back: The most frequent value
subdeck_path: AQA A-level Geography 7037 – Key content::Geographical skills and fieldwork::Geographical skills checklist::3.4.2.4 Statistical skills

front: Why is the median often better than the mean for data with extreme values?
back: The median is not affected by outliers
subdeck_path: AQA A-level Geography 7037 – Key content::Geographical skills and fieldwork::Geographical skills checklist::3.4.2.4 Statistical skills

front: Which measure of central tendency suits nominal (category) data?
back: The mode
subdeck_path: AQA A-level Geography 7037 – Key content::Geographical skills and fieldwork::Geographical skills checklist::3.4.2.4 Statistical skills

front: Worked example: what is the mean of 3, 5, 7, 9 and 11?
subdeck_path: AQA A-level Geography 7037 – Key content::Geographical skills and fieldwork::Geographical skills checklist::3.4.2.4 Statistical skills

front: Worked example: what is the median of 2, 4, 6 and 8?
subdeck_path: AQA A-level Geography 7037 – Key content::Geographical skills and fieldwork::Geographical skills checklist::3.4.2.4 Statistical skills

front: Worked example: what is the mode of 4, 6, 6, 6, 9 and 9?
subdeck_path: AQA A-level Geography 7037 – Key content::Geographical skills and fieldwork::Geographical skills checklist::3.4.2.4 Statistical skills

front: What is the range?
back: The highest value minus the lowest value
subdeck_path: AQA A-level Geography 7037 – Key content::Geographical skills and fieldwork::Geographical skills checklist::3.4.2.4 Statistical skills

front: Give one limitation of the range as a measure of dispersion.
back: It is distorted by one extreme value
subdeck_path: AQA A-level Geography 7037 – Key content::Geographical skills and fieldwork::Geographical skills checklist::3.4.2.4 Statistical skills

front: Worked example: what is the range of 12, 3, 27 and 8?
subdeck_path: AQA A-level Geography 7037 – Key content::Geographical skills and fieldwork::Geographical skills checklist::3.4.2.4 Statistical skills

front: What is the interquartile range?
back: The upper quartile minus the lower quartile
subdeck_path: AQA A-level Geography 7037 – Key content::Geographical skills and fieldwork::Geographical skills checklist::3.4.2.4 Statistical skills

front: What part of a data set does the interquartile range describe?
back: The spread of the middle 50% of values
subdeck_path: AQA A-level Geography 7037 – Key content::Geographical skills and fieldwork::Geographical skills checklist::3.4.2.4 Statistical skills

front: Give one strength of the interquartile range over the range.
back: It is not affected by extreme values
subdeck_path: AQA A-level Geography 7037 – Key content::Geographical skills and fieldwork::Geographical skills checklist::3.4.2.4 Statistical skills

front: Worked example: what is the interquartile range of 1, 3, 5, 7, 9, 11 and 13?
back: 8 (upper quartile 11 minus lower quartile 3)
subdeck_path: AQA A-level Geography 7037 – Key content::Geographical skills and fieldwork::Geographical skills checklist::3.4.2.4 Statistical skills

front: What does standard deviation measure?
back: The average spread of values around the mean
subdeck_path: AQA A-level Geography 7037 – Key content::Geographical skills and fieldwork::Geographical skills checklist::3.4.2.4 Statistical skills

front: What does a small standard deviation show?
back: Values are clustered closely around the mean
subdeck_path: AQA A-level Geography 7037 – Key content::Geographical skills and fieldwork::Geographical skills checklist::3.4.2.4 Statistical skills

front: What does a large standard deviation show?
back: Values are widely spread from the mean
subdeck_path: AQA A-level Geography 7037 – Key content::Geographical skills and fieldwork::Geographical skills checklist::3.4.2.4 Statistical skills

front: In the standard deviation formula used on AQA papers, what is divided by n before taking the square root?
back: The sum of (x minus mean) squared
subdeck_path: AQA A-level Geography 7037 – Key content::Geographical skills and fieldwork::Geographical skills checklist::3.4.2.4 Statistical skills

front: In a normal distribution, roughly what percentage of values lie within 1 standard deviation of the mean?
back: About 68%
subdeck_path: AQA A-level Geography 7037 – Key content::Geographical skills and fieldwork::Geographical skills checklist::3.4.2.4 Statistical skills

front: Worked example: what is the standard deviation (dividing by n) of 2, 4, 4, 4, 5, 5, 7 and 9?
back: 2 (mean 5, sum of squared deviations 32, 32/8 = 4, square root 2)
subdeck_path: AQA A-level Geography 7037 – Key content::Geographical skills and fieldwork::Geographical skills checklist::3.4.2.4 Statistical skills

front: What does Spearman's rank correlation test?
back: The strength and direction of the relationship between two variables
subdeck_path: AQA A-level Geography 7037 – Key content::Geographical skills and fieldwork::Geographical skills checklist::3.4.2.4 Statistical skills

front: What type of data does Spearman's rank use?
back: Paired data converted to ranks
subdeck_path: AQA A-level Geography 7037 – Key content::Geographical skills and fieldwork::Geographical skills checklist::3.4.2.4 Statistical skills

front: What is the formula for Spearman's rank correlation coefficient?
back: rs = 1 - (6 x sum of d squared) / (n cubed - n)
subdeck_path: AQA A-level Geography 7037 – Key content::Geographical skills and fieldwork::Geographical skills checklist::3.4.2.4 Statistical skills

front: In the Spearman's rank formula, what is d?
back: The difference between the two ranks for each pair
subdeck_path: AQA A-level Geography 7037 – Key content::Geographical skills and fieldwork::Geographical skills checklist::3.4.2.4 Statistical skills

front: In the Spearman's rank formula, what is n?
back: The number of pairs of data
subdeck_path: AQA A-level Geography 7037 – Key content::Geographical skills and fieldwork::Geographical skills checklist::3.4.2.4 Statistical skills

front: Between which values does Spearman's rank coefficient always lie?
back: -1 and +1
subdeck_path: AQA A-level Geography 7037 – Key content::Geographical skills and fieldwork::Geographical skills checklist::3.4.2.4 Statistical skills

front: What does a Spearman's rank value of +1 mean?
back: Perfect positive correlation
subdeck_path: AQA A-level Geography 7037 – Key content::Geographical skills and fieldwork::Geographical skills checklist::3.4.2.4 Statistical skills

front: What does a Spearman's rank value of -1 mean?
back: Perfect negative correlation
subdeck_path: AQA A-level Geography 7037 – Key content::Geographical skills and fieldwork::Geographical skills checklist::3.4.2.4 Statistical skills

front: What does a Spearman's rank value close to 0 mean?
back: No correlation
subdeck_path: AQA A-level Geography 7037 – Key content::Geographical skills and fieldwork::Geographical skills checklist::3.4.2.4 Statistical skills

front: Worked example: for 5 pairs with sum of d squared = 4, what is Spearman's rs?
subdeck_path: AQA A-level Geography 7037 – Key content::Geographical skills and fieldwork::Geographical skills checklist::3.4.2.4 Statistical skills

front: Worked example: for 5 pairs with sum of d squared = 40, what is Spearman's rs?
subdeck_path: AQA A-level Geography 7037 – Key content::Geographical skills and fieldwork::Geographical skills checklist::3.4.2.4 Statistical skills

front: When ranking, how are tied values ranked?
back: Each gets the average of the ranks they would share
subdeck_path: AQA A-level Geography 7037 – Key content::Geographical skills and fieldwork::Geographical skills checklist::3.4.2.4 Statistical skills

front: Worked example: ranking 10, 8, 8 and 5 from highest, what rank do the two 8s get?
back: 2.5 each
subdeck_path: AQA A-level Geography 7037 – Key content::Geographical skills and fieldwork::Geographical skills checklist::3.4.2.4 Statistical skills

front: How do you test whether a Spearman's rank result is significant?
back: Compare rs with the critical value for n in a significance table
subdeck_path: AQA A-level Geography 7037 – Key content::Geographical skills and fieldwork::Geographical skills checklist::3.4.2.4 Statistical skills

front: When is a Spearman's rank result significant?
back: When rs (ignoring its sign) is equal to or above the critical value
subdeck_path: AQA A-level Geography 7037 – Key content::Geographical skills and fieldwork::Geographical skills checklist::3.4.2.4 Statistical skills

front: What does the chi-squared test assess?
back: Whether observed frequencies differ significantly from expected frequencies
subdeck_path: AQA A-level Geography 7037 – Key content::Geographical skills and fieldwork::Geographical skills checklist::3.4.2.4 Statistical skills

front: What is the formula for chi-squared?
back: Sum of (O - E) squared / E
subdeck_path: AQA A-level Geography 7037 – Key content::Geographical skills and fieldwork::Geographical skills checklist::3.4.2.4 Statistical skills

front: In the chi-squared formula, what are O and E?
back: Observed and expected frequencies
subdeck_path: AQA A-level Geography 7037 – Key content::Geographical skills and fieldwork::Geographical skills checklist::3.4.2.4 Statistical skills

front: What type of data does the chi-squared test need?
back: Frequencies (counts) in categories, not percentages
subdeck_path: AQA A-level Geography 7037 – Key content::Geographical skills and fieldwork::Geographical skills checklist::3.4.2.4 Statistical skills

front: In a chi-squared test, what is the minimum expected frequency usually required in each category?
subdeck_path: AQA A-level Geography 7037 – Key content::Geographical skills and fieldwork::Geographical skills checklist::3.4.2.4 Statistical skills

front: How are degrees of freedom found for a chi-squared contingency table?
back: (rows - 1) x (columns - 1)
subdeck_path: AQA A-level Geography 7037 – Key content::Geographical skills and fieldwork::Geographical skills checklist::3.4.2.4 Statistical skills

front: How are degrees of freedom found for a one-row chi-squared test with k categories?
subdeck_path: AQA A-level Geography 7037 – Key content::Geographical skills and fieldwork::Geographical skills checklist::3.4.2.4 Statistical skills

front: Worked example: how many degrees of freedom does a 3 row by 4 column chi-squared table have?
subdeck_path: AQA A-level Geography 7037 – Key content::Geographical skills and fieldwork::Geographical skills checklist::3.4.2.4 Statistical skills

front: Worked example: observed counts 30 and 10, expected 20 and 20. What is chi-squared?
subdeck_path: AQA A-level Geography 7037 – Key content::Geographical skills and fieldwork::Geographical skills checklist::3.4.2.4 Statistical skills

front: What is the critical value of chi-squared at 1 degree of freedom and 0.05 significance?
subdeck_path: AQA A-level Geography 7037 – Key content::Geographical skills and fieldwork::Geographical skills checklist::3.4.2.4 Statistical skills

front: When is a chi-squared result significant?
back: When it is equal to or above the critical value
subdeck_path: AQA A-level Geography 7037 – Key content::Geographical skills and fieldwork::Geographical skills checklist::3.4.2.4 Statistical skills

front: What does the Mann-Whitney U test assess?
back: Whether two independent samples differ significantly
subdeck_path: AQA A-level Geography 7037 – Key content::Geographical skills and fieldwork::Geographical skills checklist::3.4.2.4 Statistical skills

front: What is the formula for U1 in the Mann-Whitney U test?
subdeck_path: AQA A-level Geography 7037 – Key content::Geographical skills and fieldwork::Geographical skills checklist::3.4.2.4 Statistical skills

front: In the Mann-Whitney U formula, what is R1?
back: The sum of the ranks of sample 1
subdeck_path: AQA A-level Geography 7037 – Key content::Geographical skills and fieldwork::Geographical skills checklist::3.4.2.4 Statistical skills

front: In the Mann-Whitney U test, which U value is compared with the critical value?
back: The smaller of U1 and U2
subdeck_path: AQA A-level Geography 7037 – Key content::Geographical skills and fieldwork::Geographical skills checklist::3.4.2.4 Statistical skills

front: When is a Mann-Whitney U result significant?
back: When the smaller U is equal to or below the critical value
subdeck_path: AQA A-level Geography 7037 – Key content::Geographical skills and fieldwork::Geographical skills checklist::3.4.2.4 Statistical skills

front: Worked example: two samples of 5, sample 1 rank sum R1 = 20. What is U1?
subdeck_path: AQA A-level Geography 7037 – Key content::Geographical skills and fieldwork::Geographical skills checklist::3.4.2.4 Statistical skills

front: What does nearest neighbour analysis measure?
back: Whether a point pattern is clustered, random or regular
subdeck_path: AQA A-level Geography 7037 – Key content::Geographical skills and fieldwork::Geographical skills checklist::3.4.2.4 Statistical skills

front: What is the formula for the nearest neighbour index (Rn)?
back: Rn = 2 x mean distance x square root of (n / area)
subdeck_path: AQA A-level Geography 7037 – Key content::Geographical skills and fieldwork::Geographical skills checklist::3.4.2.4 Statistical skills

front: What nearest neighbour index value shows a perfectly clustered pattern?
subdeck_path: AQA A-level Geography 7037 – Key content::Geographical skills and fieldwork::Geographical skills checklist::3.4.2.4 Statistical skills

front: What nearest neighbour index value shows a random pattern?
subdeck_path: AQA A-level Geography 7037 – Key content::Geographical skills and fieldwork::Geographical skills checklist::3.4.2.4 Statistical skills

front: What nearest neighbour index value shows a perfectly regular (uniform) pattern?
subdeck_path: AQA A-level Geography 7037 – Key content::Geographical skills and fieldwork::Geographical skills checklist::3.4.2.4 Statistical skills

front: Worked example: mean nearest neighbour distance 1 km, 25 points, area 100 km squared. What is Rn?
back: 1.0, a random pattern
subdeck_path: AQA A-level Geography 7037 – Key content::Geographical skills and fieldwork::Geographical skills checklist::3.4.2.4 Statistical skills

front: Worked example: mean nearest neighbour distance 0.1 km, 25 points, area 100 km squared. What is Rn?
back: 0.1, a clustered pattern
subdeck_path: AQA A-level Geography 7037 – Key content::Geographical skills and fieldwork::Geographical skills checklist::3.4.2.4 Statistical skills

front: What does the Gini coefficient measure?
back: Inequality in a distribution, such as income
subdeck_path: AQA A-level Geography 7037 – Key content::Geographical skills and fieldwork::Geographical skills checklist::3.4.2.4 Statistical skills

front: What Gini coefficient value means perfect equality?
subdeck_path: AQA A-level Geography 7037 – Key content::Geographical skills and fieldwork::Geographical skills checklist::3.4.2.4 Statistical skills

front: What Gini coefficient value means perfect inequality?
back: 1 (or 100 when written as a percentage)
subdeck_path: AQA A-level Geography 7037 – Key content::Geographical skills and fieldwork::Geographical skills checklist::3.4.2.4 Statistical skills

front: From which graph is the Gini coefficient derived?
back: The Lorenz curve
subdeck_path: AQA A-level Geography 7037 – Key content::Geographical skills and fieldwork::Geographical skills checklist::3.4.2.4 Statistical skills

front: What is a null hypothesis?
back: A statement that there is no significant relationship or difference
subdeck_path: AQA A-level Geography 7037 – Key content::Geographical skills and fieldwork::Geographical skills checklist::3.4.2.4 Statistical skills

front: What is an alternative hypothesis?
back: A statement that there is a significant relationship or difference
subdeck_path: AQA A-level Geography 7037 – Key content::Geographical skills and fieldwork::Geographical skills checklist::3.4.2.4 Statistical skills

front: What happens to the null hypothesis when a test result is significant?
back: It is rejected
subdeck_path: AQA A-level Geography 7037 – Key content::Geographical skills and fieldwork::Geographical skills checklist::3.4.2.4 Statistical skills

front: What does a significance level of 0.05 mean?
back: A 5% probability the result occurred by chance (95% confidence)
subdeck_path: AQA A-level Geography 7037 – Key content::Geographical skills and fieldwork::Geographical skills checklist::3.4.2.4 Statistical skills

front: What does a significance level of 0.01 mean?
back: A 1% probability the result occurred by chance (99% confidence)
subdeck_path: AQA A-level Geography 7037 – Key content::Geographical skills and fieldwork::Geographical skills checklist::3.4.2.4 Statistical skills

front: What is the minimum significance level usually accepted in geography?
back: 0.05 (95% confidence)
subdeck_path: AQA A-level Geography 7037 – Key content::Geographical skills and fieldwork::Geographical skills checklist::3.4.2.4 Statistical skills

front: What are degrees of freedom in a statistical test?
back: The number of values free to vary, used to choose the critical value
subdeck_path: AQA A-level Geography 7037 – Key content::Geographical skills and fieldwork::Geographical skills checklist::3.4.2.4 Statistical skills

front: What is a critical value?
back: The value from a table that a test result must reach to be significant
subdeck_path: AQA A-level Geography 7037 – Key content::Geographical skills and fieldwork::Geographical skills checklist::3.4.2.4 Statistical skills

front: What is a GIS (geographical information system)?
back: A computer system to capture, store, analyse and display located data
subdeck_path: AQA A-level Geography 7037 – Key content::Geographical skills and fieldwork::Geographical skills checklist::3.4.2.5 ICT skills

front: How does a GIS organise different data sets?
back: As layers that can be overlaid
subdeck_path: AQA A-level Geography 7037 – Key content::Geographical skills and fieldwork::Geographical skills checklist::3.4.2.5 ICT skills

front: What is remote sensing?
back: Collecting data about the Earth from a distance, such as by satellite
subdeck_path: AQA A-level Geography 7037 – Key content::Geographical skills and fieldwork::Geographical skills checklist::3.4.2.5 ICT skills

front: Name one source of remotely sensed data.
back: Satellite images (also: aerial photographs, drone images)
subdeck_path: AQA A-level Geography 7037 – Key content::Geographical skills and fieldwork::Geographical skills checklist::3.4.2.5 ICT skills

front: What is crowd sourcing of data?
back: Collecting data from large numbers of the public, often online
subdeck_path: AQA A-level Geography 7037 – Key content::Geographical skills and fieldwork::Geographical skills checklist::3.4.2.5 ICT skills

front: Give one limitation of crowd-sourced data.
back: Its accuracy is hard to check
subdeck_path: AQA A-level Geography 7037 – Key content::Geographical skills and fieldwork::Geographical skills checklist::3.4.2.5 ICT skills

front: What is big data?
back: Extremely large data sets, such as phone location data, analysed by computer
subdeck_path: AQA A-level Geography 7037 – Key content::Geographical skills and fieldwork::Geographical skills checklist::3.4.2.5 ICT skills

front: What is an electronic database?
back: An organised store of data held on a computer that can be searched
subdeck_path: AQA A-level Geography 7037 – Key content::Geographical skills and fieldwork::Geographical skills checklist::3.4.2.5 ICT skills

front: What is GPS used for in fieldwork?
back: Recording the exact location of data points
subdeck_path: AQA A-level Geography 7037 – Key content::Geographical skills and fieldwork::Geographical skills checklist::3.4.2.5 ICT skills

front: What is the difference between raster and vector data in GIS?
back: Raster is a grid of cells, vector uses points, lines and polygons
subdeck_path: AQA A-level Geography 7037 – Key content::Geographical skills and fieldwork::Geographical skills checklist::3.4.2.5 ICT skills

front: Give one strength of using ICT to produce graphs and statistics.
back: It is fast and reduces calculation errors
subdeck_path: AQA A-level Geography 7037 – Key content::Geographical skills and fieldwork::Geographical skills checklist::3.4.2.5 ICT skills
